title: gate_bash __init__ optional-call chain caught reportOptionalCall x3
body: The `pag() if _PAG_AVAILABLE else None` tail-conditional form makes basedpyright evaluate the call at a position where the callee can still be Optional (module flag is not a type guard), yielding reportOptionalCall on three star-import guards. Structural fix: None-guard if-form `if _X_AVAILABLE: self.x = x() else: self.x = None`. Suppression would have hidden three falsy-branch crashes.

title: gate_bash called nonexistent DirectMemory.record_event()
body: gate_bash recorded gate attempts with self.memory.record_event(...); DirectMemory API is record(event, payload) (direct_memory.py:714). record_event exists only on the PAMS Agent recorder, so the except Exception path swallowed AttributeError every attempt and the gate audit ledger silently lost entries. Fix call target only; do not rename surrounding flow labels (note_failure kept as-is).

title: emoji_maker main() dispatch was return-shadowed by mangled indentation
body: An earlier automated edit collapsed the CLI dispatch into an accidental right-shifted chain after an early `return` (emoji_maker.py L531): only `--json` remained reachable and `elif emotion:` referenced an unbound name (NameError class edge picked up as reportUndefinedVariable x3 by the checker). Every flag path (--css/--mood/--blend/--reaction) crashed at runtime while the module still imported cleanly. Fix: flattening the dispatch restored all user paths; verified by smoke against real CLI invocations.

title: emotion_blend raised TypeError on set(EmojiDef) unhashable
body: emotion_blend deduped matches with set(EmojiDef) but EmojiDef is a non-frozen dataclass and unhashable, so `--blend happy sad` raised TypeError on the user path. Fix: id()-based dedupe; behavior-equivalent (first occurrence wins). Root cause is a frozen-ness assumption never verified by a caller.

title: PYTHON_MANAGER._parse_version crashed on 3.15.0rc3 production entry
body: Naive chunking fed '0rc3' to int(), raising ValueError during _discover_installations, so PythonManager() could not instantiate at all against the production 3.15.0rc3 registry entry — months of legacy usage dead on arrival. Fix: per-chunk leading-digit extraction tolerating rc/dev suffixes; verified (3.15.0rc3)->(3,15,0), (3.11.14)->(3,11,14), plus get_by_version counts in smoke.

title: Smoke probes must use enum values from source, never guesses
body: The --mood smoke stage used a guessed value 'social' and died with SystemExit: 2 mid-harness. Reading class Mood at emoji_maker.py:50 shows the real values positive/negative/neutral/energetic/calm. Rule: before probing a CLI that validates against an Enum, transcribe the accepted values from the producer's source (same discipline as VERIFY ORACLES fixture capture).

title: Harness only catches BaseException: SystemExit otherwise kills quietly
body: The smoke harness died rc=2 with no stage output because stage() caught only Exception while argparse errors raise SystemExit, a BaseException subclass. Harness catch blocks should be except BaseException so every stage reports; production code must not copy this (swallowing SystemExit is a violation there).

title: Sentinel policy blocks temp-dir writes: assert without writing
body: Re-encoding a save_inventory() smoke stage as a temp-file write was rejected by sentinel_enforcer policy (PermissionError: unauthorized write). The stage was rewritten as non-writing assertions (parse-version parity, get_default/get_azazael_venv truthiness, get_by_version counts) instead of fighting the policy or probing against the real project dir.

title: Whole-tree pool numbers drift behind moving HEAD mid-lane
body: Lane plan assumed 302E/70W (baseline at a459ec36) but a fresh whole-tree run returned 275E/63W because Beam's slice #1601 landed 78c1e578 upstream mid-lane, clearing ~17E. Always re-derive git HEAD and re-run the whole-tree report immediately before landing; never carry a pool witness across a moving base when claiming numbers.

title: AP-5 violation: want-me-to phrasing for mandated follow-up actions
body: transcript_ap5_gate flagged two real violations from my own emitted prose (opencode ses_eb6edc41): offering to mint gates with WANT-ME-TO phrasing — mandated lane actions are not requests, they are obligations to execute. The gate is post-hoc only; the only available control is self-discipline in future turns: assert the next mandated step and execute it, never ask permission.

title: Manifest stamps can post-date graph.json content: verify selection via git range, not detect-sha
body: Refresh #1602 verification near-miss: save_manifest stamps rows (ast_hash set, seen=1792623300) at manifest-write time, which can post-date graph.json node content, so a .graphify_detect.json sha-diff alone reads stale payloads as current. Freshness was instead established from `git diff 78c1e578..HEAD --name-only` (trio-only changed-code subset at HEAD dffff187) plus a direct on-disk read (built_at_commit=dffff1879af5… at graph.json:1507074). Earlier direct probe printed ast_hash=None/seen=None — a wrong nested-shape assumption in the probe, not a data defect; validate probe shape against producer source before trusting its output.

title: pwsh heredoc + here-string python -c quoting failures
body: Two parallel shell probes failed: pwsh has no <<EOF heredoc (python -u - <<'EOF' -> ParserError 'Missing file specification after redirection operator'), and double-quoted here-strings (@"..."@) pass backslash-escapes literally into python -c, so embedded \" inside f-strings raised SyntaxError. Fix shape: write probe scripts as files under C:/Users/clint/AppData/Local/Temp/opencode/ and run those; reserve python -c one-liners for quote-free code only.

title: basedpyright report JSON shape: flat ids, no positions
body: logs/basedpyright_report.json written by tools/type_check_gate.py stores findings as diagnostic_ids strings of the form 'relfile:rule:message' with no line/col fields, plus summary and severity aggregates. Per-file counts need split(':', 2) parsing, and line-precise locations require a separate basedpyright --outputjson probe run over an explicit target list. Built C:/Users/clint/AppData/Local/Temp/opencode/pool_probe.py to do both when planning slices.

title: register_worm import-line assignment type: fallback declares the binding
body: 54 reportAssignmentType findings across src/CORE/WORMS/* flag the import line 'from CORE.worm_registry import register_worm' because the except-branch fallback def register_worm(**kw): ... types the module binding as (**kw)->((cls)->Unknown); the real decorator's explicit-kwargs signature (category/priority/cooldown_seconds/description/tags per worm_registry.py:443, returns (cls)->type) is not assignable to a wildcard-kwargs callable. Structural fix per file: mirror the real signature's named kwargs in the fallback so import line and fallback agree; verify empirically on one file before pattern-rolling.

title: Docstring-swallowed import in VIDEO_ANALYZER_WORM
body: VIDEO_ANALYZER_WORM.py L20 carries 'import argparse' as DOCSTRING CONTENT inside the Usage example block; the real stdlib import is absent, so both argparse references (L517 parser construction, L519 formatter_class) were undefined for the file's whole life. Fixed by deleting the stray docstring line and adding 'import argparse' to the true import block (L33). Anti-pattern class: code text hidden inside documentation blocks survives every runtime check because the module __main__ CLI path is never exercised by tests.

title: berks _record hasattr('record') guard dead - PamsRecorder API is record_event
body: berks.py:198 guarded p.record with hasattr(p, 'record') but CORE/PamsRecorder.py:207 exposes record_event(event_type, data, source, severity, tags). The guard was never satisfiable, so monitoring records were silently dropped for the worm's whole life. Structural fix: guard hasattr(p, 'record_event') and call p.record_event(event_type, data). Related typing miss: _get_pams() in BINARY_ANALYSIS_TYPES.py is un-annotated, so the caller at BINARY_ANALYSIS_TOOLS.py:47 saw Literal[True] instead of PamsRecorder; annotate return as PamsRecorder | None via a TYPE_CHECKING import.

title: lazy_replan compute_incremental_replan: no return, zero callers
body: compute_incremental_replan declares -> PlanState (lazy_replan.py:189) and the body ends after the first_diff/last_diff scan loop at file EOF with no return statement, so it returns None on every path. Grep found zero callers across src/, which is why the contract violation never surfaced at runtime. Fix: write the padded new_steps into self.plan_state.steps and return self.plan_state per the docstring contract - minimal completion, no invented branch logic. Verified the file ends mid-function (215 lines, for-loop is the last statement).

title: Re-tripped cached lesson g1613-01: pwsh heredoc attempted again
body: Mid-lane I invoked 'python - <<'PYEOF'' in pwsh once more despite my own harvested lesson g1613-01 (no pwsh heredocs; write probe scripts as files). The call failed with ParserError 'Missing file specification after redirection operator' exactly as documented, and I immediately switched to the lesson's file-script pattern (worm_clsattrs.py). Recorded as a violation because the lesson was cached AND surfaced at lane start; the recover sequence was 1 call wasted vs prior sessions' multi-call quagmires.
